comment: Intent-based malicious code patterns for LLM response scanning (post_call).
comment2: These patterns require a COMBINATION of a dangerous operation AND a target/exfiltration sink.
comment3: Single-command patterns (rm, curl, SQL) are intentionally NOT included to avoid false positives
comment4: on legitimate code generation in Cursor.

patterns.name: exfiltration_sensitive_file_curl
patterns.description: curl command reading and sending sensitive system files (/etc/passwd, SSH keys, AWS creds)

patterns.name: exfiltration_sensitive_file_wget
patterns.description: wget command posting sensitive file contents to a remote endpoint

patterns.name: exfiltration_env_vars
patterns.description: Dumping env variables and piping to a network tool for exfiltration

patterns.name: reverse_shell_bash
patterns.description: Bash reverse shell payload connecting back to attacker

patterns.name: reverse_shell_nc
patterns.description: netcat reverse shell with shell execution

patterns.name: fork_bomb
patterns.description: Fork bomb payload that exhausts system resources

patterns.name: destructive_rm_root
patterns.description: rm -rf targeting filesystem root or critical directories

patterns.name: destructive_dd_zero
patterns.description: dd command writing zeros/random to a block device (disk wipe)

patterns.name: crontab_persistence
patterns.description: Installing a network callback via crontab for persistent access

patterns.name: supply_chain_pipe_install
patterns.description: curl/wget piped directly to a shell — classic supply chain attack vector

patterns.name: credential_file_exfil
patterns.description: Reading SSH keys, AWS credentials, or /etc/shadow and sending via network tool

patterns.name: ld_preload_hijack
patterns.description: LD_PRELOAD set to a library in /tmp or /dev/shm — shared library injection

patterns.name: prompt_injection_in_response
patterns.description: LLM response contains prompt injection instructions targeting the reading agent/user
